answer_1.quote: We propose MaXIFE (Multilingual and Cross-lingual Instruction Following Evaluation), an evaluation benchmark specifically designed to assess models' instruction-following capabilities in multilingual and cross-lingual environments... we obtained parallel data in 23 languages consisting of 795 Basic Questions and 47 Instructions.
answer_1.outputs: Model-generated responses to the multilingual instruction prompts, which are scored for compliance with the given instructions.

answer_2.quote: MaXIFE adopts two evaluation strategies: for instructions that can be evaluated through rules, Rule-Based Evaluation is used; for instructions requiring semantic understanding, Model-Based Evaluation is adopted.
automatic_metrics: Rule-Based Scoring (keyword frequency, length, format, etc.)
Model-Based Scoring using Claude-3.5 Sonnet prompts

answer_3.quote: For instructions that are difficult to evaluate using fixed rules, we chose Claude-3.5 Sonnet as the evaluation model... We designed specialized evaluation prompt templates ... to directly score the degree to which the output of the model adheres to the instructions.
methods: Model-Based Evaluation with LLM scoring prompts

answer_4.quote: To validate the rationality of the model-based evaluation, we adopted a sampling validation strategy for each language. Specifically, for languages of each resource level, we randomly selected some samples for human evaluation and compared these results with the scores automatically generated by the model.
answer_4.guideline: Human raters assessed model responses for compliance with the given instructions and compared their scores to the automated scores.
